aggregation.name: Aggregation
aggregation.description: A system evolves from a single element to several, then many, finally an integrated whole.
stages: Mono — a single element performs the function.
Bi — two similar elements cooperate.
Poly — many similar or diverse elements.
Integrated system — the elements functionally merge into one unit.

dynamism.name: Dynamism
dynamism.description: Rigid systems become increasingly mobile — up to dissolution into a field.
stages: Rigid — fixed shape, no motion.
Jointed — discrete joints enable single degrees of freedom.
Elastic — continuous deformation (springs, membranes).
Fluid / powdery — formless, freely flowing.
Field — the mechanical substance disappears, a field acts (magnetic, electric, acoustic …).

scale.name: Scale
scale.description: The working level of the system shifts to ever smaller structures.
stages: Macro — parts in cm to m range.
Meso — structures in mm range.
Micro — μm structures (MEMS, microfluidics).
Nano / molecular — direct manipulation of individual molecules / atoms.

automation.name: Automation
automation.description: Human intervention is progressively replaced by machine, control loop, and finally autonomy.
stages: Manual — human operates directly.
Mechanised — tool amplifies human force / precision.
Automatic — fixed sequence without intervention in normal operation.
Autonomous — system decides on its own, learns, adapts.

completeness.name: Completeness
completeness.description: A technical system gradually internalises all four sub-functions: engine / transmission / tool / control.
stages: Tool — passive component, external energy source.
+ Transmission — power transmission integrated.
+ Engine — energy conversion on board.
+ Control — complete system with feedback loop.

controllability.name: Controllability
controllability.description: From open, uncalibrated operation to learning feedback loops.
stages: Open loop — no feedback, fixed set-point.
Measured — sensor delivers actual value, operator corrects.
Adaptive control — closed loop adjusts actuation automatically.
Smart — learning loop, model-predictive, context-aware.

matching.name: Niche matching
matching.description: From universal mass product to self-adapting system.
stages: Universal — one size fits all.
Adjustable — discrete settings chosen by the user.
Individually fitted — custom-made per user / application.
Self-adapting — system adjusts to user / environment automatically.

uneven.name: Uneven development
uneven.description: Which subsystem lags and limits the whole? The classical bottleneck phenomenon.

usage.intro: Qprovement is a browser-based Six Sigma toolkit. This surface reads the project state, adds tools and calls their actions — through the same calls the user interface uses.
usage.call: window.qprovement.interact() returns this description. window.qprovement.interact(action) or interact([action, …]) executes and returns a Promise.
usage.actionForm: An action is { op, … } with the fields from the action catalog. Unknown fields are an error. Giving an action its own id makes it referenceable.
usage.refForm: A reference to an earlier result is the object { $from: '<id>', path: '<dot-path>' }. The path knows keys and numeric indices only — no arithmetic, no filters. If you need to compute, read and send a second batch.
usage.nullableForm: In a result shape, { $nullable: … } means “this shape or null at runtime”. $nullable is a word of the grammar, not a key — reference the field itself and branch in a second batch instead of descending into the shape.
usage.batchForm: The whole batch is validated before anything runs. On the first runtime error execution stops; partial results already obtained are returned.
usage.errorForm: Each entry returns { ok: true, result } or { ok: false, error, message, available? }. available names the valid alternatives.
usage.availability: Modules without a release appear in the catalog with available: false. They are described but not operable — tell the user which tool would be right now and let them drive it.
usage.limits: You get numbers, not pictures: you cannot see a chart. There is no undo — the user was prompted to export when granting access.
usage.viewSwitch: instance.call shows the target instance before calling its method — the viewmodel only lives in the active view. A batch that calls several instances switches the view accordingly; that is intended, and it is how the user sees what is being worked on.
